alt: Valuable resources and remoteness or scenery draw five activities: resource extraction, tourism, irrigation agriculture, infrastructure and research stations. Each brings people, roads, waste and water demand into a fragile system that cannot absorb much disturbance.
caption: Resources and scenery draw people in; fragile systems cannot absorb what they bring.

alt: Climate variability and human activity (overgrazing, over-cultivation, removing woody vegetation for fuel and poor irrigation that salinises soil) interact to cause desertification, the degradation of land in drylands. It is not simply a desert advancing on its own.
caption: Desertification needs both climate variability and human misuse of dryland.

after: ### Engineering on permafrost: the Trans-Alaska Pipeline
alt: Cross-section of the raised Trans-Alaska Pipeline. The hot oil pipe sits on a crossbeam between vertical supports fitted with heat pipes that carry heat out of the ground in winter, keeping ice-rich permafrost frozen. Caribou pass underneath. A plan view shows the zigzag route from Prudhoe Bay to Valdez.
caption: Raised supports and heat pipes keep the permafrost frozen beneath a hot-oil pipeline.

alt: A chain from low productivity and harsh conditions to slow regrowth of vegetation and soils to long-lasting damage. Below, a tundra cross-section shows two tyre ruts that stay bare, with the ground beneath them thawing more deeply than the surrounding ground.
caption: Slow regrowth means damage, such as tyre tracks on tundra, can last for many years.
